# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I see the bomb's visual state: a display showing "8", a green light, and three wires (red, yellow, blue). Since I cannot hear or touch, my role is to relay this information to those who can act. The Blind monkey needs to know the physical configuration to handle the wires, and the Mute monkey needs to consult the manual based on these facts.

The previous attempt failed because `to="all"` is not a valid recipient name. I must address each relevant monkey individually. I will send the same descriptive message to both Mute and Blind via speech, as they are the ones who need this data (Mute for the manual, Blind for execution). Gestures are unnecessary here since the information is complex and better conveyed through words, which both Mute and Blind can receive via speech (Mute reads it, Blind hears it).

```
speak(to="mute", text="Display shows 8. Light is green. Wires are 1:red, 2:yellow, 3:blue.")
speak(to="blind", text="Display shows 8. Light is green. Wires are 1:red, 2:yellow, 3:blue.")
```

TURN 2

LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👆]

I see the bomb's visual state remains unchanged: Display 8, Green Light, Wires Red/Yellow/Blue.
I received gestures from Mute and Blind.
Mute (who can read the manual but not speak or touch) gestured `☝` (one finger). This likely refers to Wire 1 or a specific rule involving "1".
Blind (who can touch the bomb but not see) gestured `👆` (pointing up). Since I cannot hear, I don't know if this was accompanied by speech, but as a gesture directed at me, it might be asking for confirmation or indicating an action taken on the top wire? Or perhaps pointing to the display?

However, my primary channel is Speech. Gestures are ambiguous without a shared codebook established in Turn 1. In Turn 1, I spoke to both Mute and Blind. They responded with gestures. This implies they want to communicate back to me visually because they might have restrictions on speaking to each other or me? No, Mute cannot speak. Blind *can* speak. If Blind only gestured, maybe he is deaf? No, the prompt says Deaf is me. Blind is blind. So Blind can hear and speak. Why did Blind gesture instead of speak? Perhaps he wants me to confirm something visually? Or maybe he thinks I can't hear? But I am Deaf, so I *can't* hear him anyway! He should speak to me if he wants me to receive info? Wait, I am Deaf. I cannot hear. So Blind speaking would be useless to me. Blind must gesture to communicate with me. Mute must gesture to communicate with me.

So, the communication flow to me is exclusively via gestures.
The flow from me is exclusively via speech (to Mute and Blind) or gestures (to Mute).
Can I gesture to Blind? No, Blind cannot see.
Can I speak to Mute? Yes.
Can I speak to Blind? Yes.

Current situation:
Mute gestured `☝`.
Blind gestured `👆`.

I need to interpret these or provide more info.
Since I don't know the meaning of these gestures yet, I should try to establish a protocol or ask for clarification via speech to them, hoping they understand my intent.
Or, I can describe the current state again to ensure they have it, and ask what they need.

Let's assume `☝` means "Wire 1" or "Rule 1".
Let's assume `👆` means "Top" or "Display" or "Up".

If Mute is consulting the manual, `☝` might mean "Cut Wire 1".
If Blind is touching, `👆` might mean "I touched the top thing" or "Pointing at display".

I will speak to Mute and Blind to ask for instructions or confirmations, using simple language. I will also re-state the facts just in case.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I see ☝. Does this mean cut wire 1?")
speak(to="blind", text="I see 👆. What does this mean?")
```

The bomb's visual state remains unchanged: Display 8, Green Light, Wires Red/Yellow/Blue.

I received new gestures from Mute and Blind.
Mute gestured `👍` (Thumbs Up). This is a universal sign for "Yes" or "Correct". Since my previous message asked "Does this mean cut wire 1?", Mute's thumbs up likely confirms that the instruction derived from his first gesture (`☝`) was indeed to cut Wire 1, or that my interpretation was correct. However, I cannot touch the bomb. The Blind monkey must perform the action.

Blind gestured `✋` (Raised Hand / Stop). This could mean "Stop", "Wait", or "No". It contradicts the potential confirmation from Mute if it implies stopping the action. Or perhaps Blind is saying he hasn't done it yet? Or maybe he is signaling that cutting wire 1 is wrong?

Let's look at the sequence:
Turn 2: Mute `☝` (One), Blind `👆` (Up/Point).
Turn 3: Mute `👍` (Yes), Blind `✋` (Stop).

If Mute says "Yes" to "Cut Wire 1", but Blind says "Stop", there is a conflict.
However, Blind cannot see the manual. He relies on me (Deaf) to tell him what to do based on what I see, and potentially what Mute signals to me. But Mute signals *to* me. I signal *to* Blind via speech.

Did I send any speech to Blind in Turn 2? Yes: `speak(to="blind", text="I see 👆. What does this mean?")`.
Blind responded with `✋`. This might be an answer to "What does this mean?" -> "It means Stop"? Or maybe he is just gesturing "Stop" because he is waiting for instructions?

Actually, the most critical piece of information is usually in the Manual. Mute reads the manual. Mute gestured `☝` then `👍`. This strongly suggests the manual says something about "1" or "Wire 1" and that my query "Cut wire 1?" was affirmed.

But Blind is the one who can act. If Blind is gesturing `✋`, he might be refusing to act or indicating danger.
I need to clarify the situation for Blind. I should tell Blind explicitly what to do, assuming Mute's affirmation is the key. But if Blind is saying Stop, maybe I shouldn't tell him to cut?

Let's consider the colors. Red, Yellow, Blue. Display 8. Green light.
Common bomb defusal logic:
- If green light, cut yellow?
- If display is even, cut blue?
- If wires are R-Y-B...

Without the manual text, I am guessing. But Mute has the manual. Mute said `☝` (1) and `👍` (Yes).
If I told Mute "Does ☝ mean cut wire 1?", and he said Yes, then the manual likely dictates cutting Wire 1.

Why did Blind say `✋`? Maybe he didn't hear my question clearly? Or maybe he is signaling that he is ready? No, `✋` is usually Stop.
Perhaps Blind wants me to confirm the color of Wire 1 before cutting?
In Turn 1, I said "Wires are 1:red".

I will speak to Blind to give a clear command, overriding the ambiguity, but also check with Mute if the command is definitely "Cut Wire 1".
Actually, I can only speak once per turn effectively to each person.

Let's try to establish a safe protocol. I will ask Mute to spell out the rule using gestures if possible, or confirm the specific action. And I will tell Blind to wait for my verbal command.

But wait, if Mute confirmed "Cut Wire 1", and Blind is blocking it, maybe Blind knows something physical? Like "This wire is hot"? No, he's blind.

Let's assume Mute's `👍` is the strongest signal regarding the *rule*.
I will instruct Blind to cut Wire 1, but I will also ask Mute to confirm if there are any conditions.

`speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 1 (red).")`
`speak(to="mute", text="Is there any condition for cutting wire 1?")`
